newsitem.title: FRANCE: Canal Plus says Premiere talks not over.
newsitem.headline: Canal Plus says Premiere talks not over.

text.p: Talks between French pay television company Canal Plus and German media group Bertelsmann over German television channel Premiere are not over, Michel Thoulouz, Canal Plus managing director for international affairs said on Friday.
"As of today the talks are not finished," Thoulouz told a Canal Plus shareholders' meeting.
Canal Plus chairman Pierre Lescure told shareholders that he would present a valuation of Canal Plus's 37.5 percent in Premiere to a Canal Plus board meeting on July 2.
Canal Plus had been involved in talks to exchange its share in Premiere against the 45 percent which Kirch holds in Italian pay television station Telepiu for months, he said.
But Canal Plus was dependent on the outcome of talks between Bertelsmann and Bavarian media magnate Leo Kirch over their respective shares in Premiere, he said.
"The value of Premiere is higher than that of Telepiu. There will be a cash sum involved," Thoulouz said.
On Monday Bertelsmann and Kirch ended a long battle for position in Premiere, saying they would become equal partners in the pay television group.

"(Bertelsmann's) CLT-UFA and the Kirch group agreed over the weekend to end the squabbles in the German pay-TV market and to pursue the development of pay TV, particularly the digital market, together," their joint statement, issued on Monday, said.
Kirch currently holds 25 percent of Premiere, while CLT-UFA, owned by Bertelsmann and GBL-Audiofina, holds the remaining 37.5 percent.
As recently as last week German media reports said Kirch wanted to buy all of the Canal Plus stake, giving it control of Premiere.
But Kirch was also said to be in financial difficulties due to high start-up costs at its DF1 digital television unit, set up to compete with Premiere.
Canal Plus already owns 45 percent of Telepiu via Nethold, which it took over in April. Buying Kirch's stake would give it 90 percent.
In that event, the French company would seek Italian investors to be its partners in Telepiu, as long as it retained a majority, a broadcasting source has said.
